title: 《卡莉亚的炼金工房》「鲁特&蕾妮雅」宣传视频
text:
前作角色已成为值得信赖的前辈们再次登场
前作《优米雅的炼金工房》中的角色将在《卡莉亚的炼金工房》成为值得信赖的前辈们再次登场。经验丰富、关键时刻值得信赖的鲁特，以及历经往昔冒险而成长，如今已成为支持后辈支柱的蕾妮雅，作为阿拉迪斯开拓团的前辈，他们一直支持着卡莉亚一行人的冒险。《卡莉亚的炼金工房 ～夜之王国与追忆之道标～》将于2027年2月25日登陆PS5、XBOX Series、Switch 2及PC平台。

title: 《Escape From Playtime》发售日预告
text:
深入废弃玩具工厂的幽暗深处
《Escape from Playtime》是一款以《波比的游戏时光》世界观为背景的合作生存恐怖游戏。深入废弃玩具工厂的幽暗深处，在潜伏于暗处的怪物手中挣扎求生。每局游戏都会将你带入不同的区域：教室、仓库、测试实验室，以及连接各处的昏暗走廊。工厂里的「居民」——那些同样被游戏时光公司淘汰的残次品，在破败的走廊里游荡，寻找下一个猎物。要想全身而退，逃出工厂，就必须与好友通力合作，巧妙利用周遭的一切。游戏将于10月21日在PC平台开启抢先体验。

title: 《检疫区：最后一站》「迈阿密零」DLC预告
text:
欢迎来到爆发的源头
欢迎来到爆发的源头：佛罗里达州迈阿密。迈阿密派对圈中越来越多的人正在分享一种新东西：一种前所未见的、能够改变基因的病毒。你是唯一的第一响应者，病毒传播之际，你要奋战在感染源头的第一线。运用一系列全新的工具和技术，评估幸存者，应对前所未见的症状。但在「迈阿密零」，守卫入口只是工作的一部分，你还需要在实验室里待上一段时间。测试潜在的治疗方法，进行人体实验，竭尽所能控制这场疫情。《检疫区：最后一站》免费DLC「迈阿密零」将于10月15日推出。

title: 《球比伦战记》「升天球比伦」DLC公布预告
text:
你能否挺身面对崛起的全新威胁？
作为《球比伦战记》迄今为止规模最庞大、玩法变化最巨大的扩展包，「升天球比伦」将带来琳琅满目的新角色、新弹珠、新被动物品、新敌人、新头目、新建筑以及新关卡，大幅扩展的内容将让每一局游戏都充满无尽坑，而全新的游戏机制甚至会考验身经百战的深渊老兵。你能否挺身面对崛起的全新威胁？《球比伦战记》「升天球比伦」DLC将于11月12日推出。

title: 《血狼》剧情预告
text:
展开一场残酷而永无止境的复仇之旅
一半是狼人，一半是吸血鬼……释放你的复仇怒火。在《血狼（Vaewolf）》这款以英格兰蛮荒北部为背景的砍杀式力量幻想游戏中，展开一场残酷而永无止境的复仇之旅，尽情释放你那永不停息的怒火。游戏将于2027年初登陆PS5、XBOX Series、Switch 2及PC平台。

title: 《要塞4》「遭遇战」预告
text:
将于2026年内登陆PC平台
感受一个鲜活的中世纪世界对你的城堡经济和攻城技艺的影响，与此同时你还要勇斗敌对的亡命徒、领主宿敌以及恶劣天气。《要塞4（Stronghold 4）》将于2026年内登陆PC平台。

title: 《矮人挖掘机》公布预告
text:
指挥矮人建造一台巨型矮人挖掘机器
指挥矮人建造一台巨型矮人挖掘机器。采集资源、寻找强大的神器、抵御敌人，在这款增量策略游戏中征服地下世界。《矮人挖掘机（Dwarven Digging Machine）》将于2027年登陆PC平台。

title: 《真菌朋克》1.0正式版发售日预告
text:
深入危险的星球任务 全力抵抗真菌浩劫
一群被淘汰的机器人被赛克森公司招募，获得了最后一次证明自己的机会——赢得荣誉并挣个盆满钵满（顺便也就不用被丢进废品堆了）。作为临时拼凑的灭菌小队——「新阿特拉斯危害处理小队」，他们受命调查一场席卷整个星球的真菌灾难背后的秘密。深入危险的星球任务，全力抵抗这场真菌浩劫。这真的只是他们所声称的一场自然灾害吗？话说赛克森公司真的弄错了你的税务申报吗？还是你自己搞砸了？《真菌朋克（Mycopunk）》1.0正式版将于10月21日登陆PS5及PC平台。

title: 《孤山独影》「循迹识踪：深水」DLC上线日期预告
text:
与专业攀岩者艾瓦一起踏上旅程
与专业攀岩者艾瓦一起踏上旅程，任意选择攀登起点，精心规划路线，管理手中的资源，在环境恶劣的神之山上生存下来。《循迹识踪》为攀岩者带来了新的攀爬地点和挑战。你可以自由探索路线，解决全新的攀爬难题，跟随传奇攀岩者的足迹，探索新的标志性地点。在《循迹识踪》系列DLC中，第一部是《深水》，为各位玩家带来了3个新的攀爬区域，还引入了水上攀岩：你现在可以在水域上空进行攀岩，不用担心掉下去摔死！「循迹识踪：深水」DLC将于10月29日推出。

title: 《WANE》公布预告
text:
深入被你的过往重新唤醒的地下城
《WANE》是一款以角色为核心的战术Roguelite。你将带领一群神秘学者，深入被你的过往重新唤醒的地下城——拉维尔。别让队伍分崩离析，在高风险的回合制战斗中活下来，还要为下一次远征筹措资金。在记忆彻底凋零之前，你能否剜除拉维尔心脏深处的腐朽？游戏将登陆PC平台，具体发售日期待定。

title: 《寂静岭：Townfall》发售预告
text:
让一切重回正轨
为了「让一切重回正轨」，西蒙·奥德尔重返坐落于岛屿的神秘小镇，一步步踏入充满着紧张周旋、激烈冲突与难解谜题的世界。而圣阿米莉亚的真相，也随之悄然浮现。《寂静岭：Townfall》将于9月24日登陆PS5及PC平台。

title: 《最终幻想 RESONANCE》最终前瞻
text:
确实让我印象深刻
《最终幻想 RESONANCE》给我的感觉就像是在走钢丝，一边要深情款款地向历代《最终幻想》致敬，一边又要开辟足够新奇有趣的新方向，并讲好自己的故事。它能稳稳走完吗？我们只能拭目以待，但就这一小时的试玩来说，它确实让我印象深刻。

title: TGS 2026《狂热运输 3》主创访谈｜IGN 中国
text:
相关文章: 《狂热运输3》发售日预告 | gamescom 2026
由瑞士开发商 Urban Games 研发、Paradox Interactive 负责发行的交通模拟经营大作《狂热运输 3》即将在 9 月 30 日正式上市。作为该系列的新起点，本作在保持了前作真实、细致且硬核的交通网搭建体验的同时，借助 Paradox 在策略模拟领域的丰富经验，正试图以更具野心也更具亲和力的姿态走向更广泛的玩家群体。
依靠在核心玩法上的极度专注，《狂热运输 2》曾拿下了全球销量超 200 万份、Steam 综合好评率近 90% 的傲人成绩，繁荣的 MOD 生态更是让其拥有了极长的生命力。 还有更多相关内容 《狂热运输3》「新功能与改进」介绍视频
如今，全面升级的《狂热运输 3》迎来了更广阔的舞台。老实说，作为一名鲜少涉猎硬核模拟经营游戏的纯新手，我最初对本作庞大的交通网络系统是抱有几分敬畏的，甚至在初步尝试中感到有些无从下手。但在本届东京电玩展 2026 的闭门交流会中，《狂热运输 3》的发行经理 Nicolas Heini 用长达一个多小时的教学，彻底打消了我的顾虑。我决定纯粹从一个新手的视角出发，去领略游戏的核心内容，看看这部新作是如何兼容并包的。
“对于《狂热运输 3》，我们的核心理念是让游戏对初次接触的玩家更具亲和力，同时又为专家级玩家保留极高的挑战性。”Nicolas Heini 一边说着，一边向我展示了游戏的基础框架。
本作的时间跨度从 1900 年一直延伸到 2030 年及以后，包含了电车、公交、火车、直升机、船只和飞机在内的 300 多种交通工具。在难度设置上，游戏给予了玩家极大的自由：你既可以将其设定为“非常困难”来挑战极限，也可以关闭所有限制，在拥有无限资金的沙盒模式下随心所欲地建造。
为了让我直观感受新作的画面与世界运转，Nicolas Heini 载入了一个游玩了三到五个小时的亚寒带植被地图。在这个类似斯堪的纳维亚半岛的地貌中，遍布着连绵的山脉、森林和沼泽，这对早期的交通网铺设提出了不小的挑战。
新作在视觉表现上有了显著的提升，最引人注目的当属全新的昼夜交替与天气系统。Nicolas Heini 强调，这完全是视觉层面的可选功能，不会对实际经济和交通流产生负面影响。你甚至可以将其设置为与你的电脑桌面本地时间同步，或者干脆关掉它以保证永远在白天施工。此外，游戏中每座城市都有近 20 个发展等级，每当城市成功升级时，天空中甚至会燃放起绚丽的烟花以示庆祝。
另外，本作中玩家不再是一个隐形的造物主，而是自由选址并建造属于自己的总部大楼。这是一个高度模块化的建筑，你可以随着进度为其添加各种装饰，甚至能在总部旁边建一个网球场。
从零开始：告别手忙脚乱的“魔法仓库”与深度产业链
开发者亲自演示了如何一步步搭建交通线。他熟练地向银行申请了贷款，在两座城市之间规划了公交站的覆盖半径，并建立了一个车辆调度站。游戏内的所有载具不仅可以自由更改颜色，玩家甚至可以切换到第一人称视角，化身公交司机，沉浸式地体验自己规划的路线。开发者甚至特意为我挑选了一列中国的高铁列车来串联起跨城客运线。
随后，演示进入了本作最具深度的货运与产业链环节。开发者顺着地图向我展示了一个复杂而迷人的闭环：首先，海上的钻井平台提取石油，由货船运往炼油厂转化为燃料；一部分燃料由卡车运往城市，另一部分则运往化工厂制成颜料；颜料随后被送往印刷厂制作成书籍，最终这些书籍被运往城市的商业区。
随着城市的扩张，市民的需求最多会增加到 6 种不同的货物。游戏细化了“城市幸福度”的概念，共有 8 个不同的评分指标。开发者指着地图上一处停止生长且标有红色警告的城市区域解释道：“你可以看到这里出了大问题，因为运到这座城市的鱼类在路上耽搁了太久，全部都不新鲜了。显然，没有人愿意吃不新鲜的鱼，这就导致了居民幸福度暴跌，城市停止了扩张。”
为了解决新手在物流调度时常常面临的货物过期焦虑，本作引入了“专业仓库”机制。在建立一条将鱼类运往城市的航线时，开发者特意建造了一个昂贵的鱼类专属仓库。他解释道，如果使用便宜的通用仓库，货物在等待转运时，其交付时间依然会流逝；但如果建造了造价昂贵的专业仓库，交货时间的流逝就会被强行暂停，让玩家能更加从容地进行车船调度。
此外，工厂的产能不再仅仅依赖于原材料的输入，本作首次引入了“员工”与“增益道具”的概念。例如，你可以专门开设一条客运线将工人送往农场，仅此一项就能提升 57% 的生产率；如果你还能将机械齿轮或肥料等特定物资运达，工厂的产能甚至能获得高达 148% 的惊人增幅。交通枢纽不再仅仅是搬运工，而是直接盘活区域经济的发动机。
而当你的公司发展到一定规模后，还能解锁独一无二的地标建筑。开发者向我展示了来自巴西的基督像，这些地标造价极高且需要海量资源，但一旦建成，就能为所在区域提供强大的永久增益，比如专门用于降低城市噪音，或者提升某类交通工具的运行速度。
属于“基建狂魔”的现代沙盒
在演示的后半段，为了展示游戏的终局潜力，开发者开启了 MOD 全部解锁的沙盒模式，将时间线直接拨到了 2030 年。在这片未来的都市中，不仅新增了直升机穿梭于高楼与海上平台之间，街头甚至跑起了特斯拉 CyberTruck、金龙客车等电动载具。沙盒模式下还会随机生成类似支线的补贴任务，完成它们可以获得丰厚的资金和加成奖励，极大丰富了长线游玩的乐趣。
开发者特别提到，他们观察到了中国玩家极具特色的游玩风格：“很多中国玩家其实并不在意 1900 年的早期马车时代，他们喜欢直接从 1990 年或 2000 年开始，在无限金钱的沙盒模式下，修建极其复杂、宏伟的现代高速公路枢纽和高铁网络。”
为了回应这份热情，他在地图上用最高级的多车道公路和高架桥，向我快速搭建了一个极具中国现代基建风格的巨大立交桥网络和拥有极长站台的枢纽火车站。在此期间甚至发生了一个有趣的小彩蛋：天空中飘过一个热气球，上面有一位 Urban Games 的开发者正在向玩家挥手致意。
开发者告诉我，为了确保首发体验，他们花费了一年多的时间与中外顶尖的 MOD 作者合作，确保游戏在首发第一天就会有近百个高质量 MOD 直接实装，彻底告别“新游戏无 MOD 可用”的空窗期。
开发者 Q&A ：关于主机版、未来载具与中国市场
在长达一小时的深入演示结束后，我向 Nicolas Heini 提出了一系列我们比较关心的问题。以下为本次闭门采访的汇总。
IGN 中国：因为这次游戏也要登陆 PS5 和 Xbox，主机版在手柄控制方面的优化做得怎么样？主机版是否也会支持键鼠模式？
A：是的，键盘和鼠标对主机玩家来说是完全可用的，你可以随时接上使用。同时，在手柄优化方面，我们并非简单地进行移植，而是拥有一个完整的主机专用 UI。所有的图标、菜单和界面都被简化并放大了，确保你即便坐在 5 米外的沙发上也能舒适地使用手柄掌控全局。另外向你透露一个保密信息：我们目前正在积极进行 Steam Deck 的掌机适配和优化，虽然还在修复一些小问题，但目前的内部版本在性能上已经表现得非常不错了，哪怕在极大的城市规模下依然能保持流畅。
IGN 中国：如果游戏运营 5 年、10 年，随着时间的推移，会有新的科技或载具不断加入吗？
开发者：这就涉及到两个方面了。首先，我们在《狂热运输 2》上提供了长达 4 年半的免费更新支持。对于新作，我们在首发后肯定也会进行大量的更新。最开始显然是集中于修复 Bug 和打磨游戏，但随后肯定会有新的载具和更多内容加入，虽然具体的时间、形式和内容目前还不能确定，但长线更新是绝对会有的。
IGN 中国：对于像我这样第一次接触这个系列的新玩家，你有什么系统性上手的建议吗？如何能让新手保持长时间游玩的动力？
开发者：我的建议是将“教程”和“战役模式”结合起来玩。教程会给你一个基础的概念，而战役模式的前四个任务会通过循序渐进的故事带你了解不同的系统。很多人觉得这游戏看起来很复杂，但你刚刚也看到了，建立一条公交线路其实只需要放四个站牌，然后把它们连起来，就这么简单。一旦你掌握了基础逻辑，上手会比想象中容易得多。至于长线动力，你会发现随着城镇的发展，新的需求、噪音和污染问题会不断出现，你总是需要不断地去优化和解决这些问题，这种正向反馈是非常激励人的。
IGN 中国：我比较好奇一点，本作共有 8 个战役任务，这些任务在地区和时间的选择上有什么特定的标准吗？
开发者：我们主要是围绕历史上一些著名的、大家喜闻乐见的大事件来虚构故事的。比如第一个战役是在新奥尔良，你需要帮助城市在遭遇大风暴后重建狂欢节的交通线；第二个是帮助瑞士阿尔卑斯山修建面向滑雪游客的铁路线；第三个带有《印第安纳琼斯》的沙漠探险风格，需要帮助卡车穿越沙漠；第四个是著名的伍德斯托克音乐节；第五个是关于挪威海域首次发现石油；第六个是在地形复杂的菲律宾群岛发展交通；第七个是在澳大利亚建立极高幸福度的大城市；而最后一个任务，则是你需要协助建造并最终发射一枚登月火箭进入太空。我们确保了这些任务能涵盖各个时代和全球各地。
IGN 中国：最后一个问题，你们是如何看待中国玩家群体的？他们和其他地区的玩家相比，在游玩想法上有什么不一样的地方吗？
开发者：首先，中国现在已经超越德国，成为我们系列数量第一大的玩家市场了，这非常不可思议。就像我之前提到的，很多中国玩家对 1990 年之后的现代基建和高铁有着独特的热情，他们能利用游戏建造出极其复杂的高速公路和让人惊叹的巨型城市，在《狂热运输 3》中由于系统升级，他们能建造的规模将远超以往。
中国社区对我们来说极其重要。为此，我们目前正在积极筹划一项工作：为整个战役模式加入全中文配音，预计将邀请 28 位不同的中文配音演员来录制，虽然还在计划阶段，但我们正在全力推进。我们非常感谢所有中国玩家过去六年来的支持，希望大家能喜欢这款打磨了许久的新作，同时也非常期待中国的 MOD 作者们这次能利用新系统创造出怎样的奇迹！
相关文章: IGN 中国专访 Urban Games 开发团队：《狂热运输 3》的 Mod 不会整合 Paradox Mods

title: 本周 Steam 值得关注的游戏 09.21 - 09.27（一）
text:
中秋假期将至，加上临近 Steam 秋促，本周又是游戏扎堆发售的一周！《守墓人 2》《控制：共振》《SILENT HILL: Townfall》等热门作品均将在本周推出。一起来看看有没有感兴趣的作品吧！
注： 本系列文章的信息主要整合自 Steam 与 SteamDB 的即将发售列表，由于 Steam 支持手动输入日期及发售、同步不及时等原因，本列表可能会遗漏收录一些作品的发售信息。如果本周有您的作品或您喜欢的作品未被列出，欢迎直接评论补充链接～～
奇迹工厂（Brave New Wonders）
关键字： 自动化、基地建设、制作
发行日期： 2026/09/21（ 中文支持 ）
百废待兴的末日后世界，作为开拓者指挥官，你将用自由的文字指令指挥自动机展开一场工厂自动化冒险之旅。积极探索，勇敢战斗，发掘遗迹，采集资源，设计自动化生产线，让你的工厂蓬勃发展，最终打造出宏伟壮观的奇迹！
病娇病毒（Yandere Virus）
关键字： 恐怖、在线合作、生存
发行日期： 2026/09/21（ 中文支持 ）
最多支持 4 人一起游玩的在线合作恐怖游戏。 无论是单人还是与同伴一起，收集“柏拉图南瓜”，拯救感染了恐怖病娇病毒的珍贵朋友吧。
今天都是腿（IGTAP: an Incremental Game That's Also a Platformer）
关键字： 增量、精确平台、自动化
发行日期： 2026/09/21（ 中文支持 ）
《今天都是腿》是融合了增量与平台跳跃的游戏。跑酷，翻墙跳，二段跳，不断解锁新技能，完成挑战，生产克隆人军团提升收益，当能源不断溢出，解锁更强大的能力开启高收益路线！无限复制你的克隆人大军！
Echoes of Mora
关键字： 剧情丰富、探索、时空旅行
发行日期： 2026/09/21（ 中文支持 ）
一个男孩失踪了。一座村庄沉入水底。而不知为何，你能触及过去。潜入莫拉村庄的沉没废墟，开启通往洪水来临前的传送门，跨越时间与莫拉分享你的发现。你所揭开的一切，或许将改变她乃至她所爱之人的命运。
Lootborne
关键字： 挂机游戏、桌面伴侣、自走棋
发行日期： 2026/09/21（ 中文支持 ）
一款盘踞在你屏幕一角的暗黑奇幻放置类 RPG。边工作边战斗、拾取战利品，打磨你的 build，触发物品组合效果，让角色不断变强。搭载异步 PvP 的挂机战斗游戏，为荣耀与战利品而战！
Happy Wheels
关键字： 鲜血、物理、动作
发行日期： 2026/09/21（暂无中文）
选择你那个准备不足的赛车手，为短暂的胜利拼命追逐，无视可能带来的严重后果。
The Rabbit Haul
关键字： 动作、轻度 Rogue、农场模拟
发行日期： 2026/09/21（暂无中文）
在《The Rabbit Haul》的世界里，你白天要打理苗圃、升级农场和技能，晚上则要赶跑爱捣乱的浣熊小队。在这款别具一格的塔防游戏中，你要大胆探索、细心策划并随机应变，才能让苗圃里的作物协同增产，并取得战斗胜利。
索拉丽斯炼成计划（Project Solaris）
关键字： 角色扮演、轻度 Rogue、回合制战术
发行日期： 2026/09/21（ 中文支持 ）
《Project Solaris：索拉丽斯炼成计划》是一款 Roguelike RPG，讲述了不成器的魔女“索拉丽斯”与小搭档“霍姆”一同努力、立志成为独当一面的魔法使的故事。
Custom Corner
关键字： 桌面伴侣、实用工具、装饰
发行日期： 2026/09/21（ 中文支持 ）
《Custom Corner》是一款在屏幕角落静静运行的温馨模拟与专注工具。使用 325 多种物品打造你的等距房间，享受 Lo-Fi 音乐。通过待办事项列表和专注计时器等小组件，在工作或放松时提升你的效率。
CITADEL
关键字： 视觉小说、选择取向、哲理
发行日期： 2026/09/21（暂无中文）
从沉睡中醒来，前往雄伟的城堡一探究竟。
Fruitbearer
关键字： 下落方块、物理、牌组构建式类 Rogue
发行日期： 2026/09/21（暂无中文）
这款游戏是对合成大西瓜风格物理解谜游戏的深刻重构，被重新打造为一款高难度、暗黑奇幻风格的 Roguelike 牌组构建游戏。化身为被遗忘的丰饶之神，你苏醒后，昔日的荣光已不复存在，如今面临着无日照的荒原与怪物。为了恢复平衡，你必须成长；为了成长，你必须做出牺牲。
Normal Golf Game
关键字： 高尔夫、物理、模拟、低容错
发行日期： 2026/09/21（暂无中文）
一款非常普通的高尔夫模拟器。想打什么就打什么，从任何地方开球。但请记住：除非 Luke Muscat 本人（《水果忍者》《疯狂喷气机》）满意，否则你别想离开。
Nine to Never
关键字： 平台解谜、休闲
发行日期： 2026/09/21（暂无中文）EA
日常是安全的，可预测的，舒适的。但如果这种舒适感背后隐藏着某种……危险呢？在这款游戏中，你的任务不仅仅是工作。探索奇异的空间，通过对话揭开隐藏的细节，并解开谜题，以发现这座建筑无尽日常背后令人不安的真相。
Backrooms: Code Yellow
关键字： 冒险、多人、探索、心理恐怖
发行日期： 2026/09/22（暂无中文）EA
一款支持 1 至 6 名玩家合作的在线游戏，玩家将与同事们一起在无限广阔的后室中展开调查并收集数据，探索，完成任务。平安归来。
Mad Metal
关键字： 车辆作战、汽车模拟、多人
发行日期： 2026/09/22（暂无中文）
一款黑暗风格的载具战斗射击游戏，你可以在人工智能主导的末日中操控时间、定制载具并肢解敌人。支持单人或与朋友在开放世界合作模式、撤离任务及死亡竞赛中并肩作战。
针影裁梦（Dressmaker）
关键字： 制作、模拟、设计与插画

title: Command a legion of robots in factory builder Brave New Wonders, launching tomorrow
text:
The best thing about machines is that they do exactly what you program them to do. The worst thing about machines is that they do exactly what you program them to do. In Brave New Wonders, releasing tomorrow, you'll build and automate a set of production lines with robots that you can write commands for.
In the launch trailer revealed at the PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct, we hear a narrator say, "Give the command, and the machines will answer." The commands you give can be written in plain English—or any language the game supports—and the game will ensure the machines obey your whims.
Wishlist Brave New Wonders on Steam
Release date: September 21, 2026
Brave New Wonders is a factory builder where you can give direct commands to your robots in plain text. The game launches tomorrow, September 21, and you can wishlist it on Steam .
Wishlist now
Rather than setting up a supply chain manually, simply tell your robots to pick up ammo from the warehouse and deliver it to the turret. The game seems to detect which words in your command are the keywords, such as locations and conditions. So, if a little lost robot wanders off and simply circles an area instead of going into it and grabbing what you need, you'll have no one but yourself to blame.
Brave New Wonders touts itself as "part factory builder, part city builder rising from the ruins." It's set in a post-apocalyptic far future, so it'll be up to you to mine and refine all the resources you'll need to rebuild society.
That's no small feat, so you won't just be building one factory or base. You'll be able to link factories and logistics routes, and even copy and paste huge layouts. Even the robots keep their instructions when you paste more, so you won't have to micromanage too much—unless you want to change their commands, of course.
This isn't a peaceful factory sim, however. Old machines roam the decimated world, so you'll need to place turrets to defend your bases and use dynamite to clear the way forward if you hope to expand into new territories.
Brave New Wonders launches tomorrow, September 21, and you can pick it up on Steam .

title: Lemonade Apocalypse has 3 simple tasks for you: Become a lemonade billionaire, 'fuel climate change,' and 'manipulate voters'
text:
I'll tell you this right now: I'm already into what Lemonade Apocalypse is putting down. Let me count the reasons. First, its PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct reveal trailer is a very fun satire of both billionaires and the billionaire-mindset podcast industrial complex. Two, I think it will tickle the parts of my brain that just loves turning numbers into bigger numbers. Three, a lemonade apocalypse sounds much preferable to the various other apocalypses that feel like they're on table for us right now.
Lemonade Apocalypse is actually a sequel to, uh, a game also called Lemonade Apocalypse. Stay with me. It's an economic simulator and incremental game where the task is to sell your soul for the dollar as quickly and dramatically as you can. "Build recipes from 70+ ingredients with evolving properties," the game's Steam page implores you, right before it also implores you to "Fuel climate change" and "Manipulate voters."
Wishlist Lemonade Apocalypse on Steam
Release date: Q1 2027
If you like anti-billionaire satire and/or turning small numbers into large ones, you're gonna want to pay attention to Lemonade Apocalypse, an incremental game that tasks you with building an economic empire on the back of a lemonade stand. You might cause climate change and irrevocably poison global politics while you do it, but hey, you'll be rich. Coming Q1 2027, wishlist it on Steam .
Wishlist now
You will go from flogging your lemonade at a street-side stand to running an all-conquering, lemon-based capitalist empire. Morals have gone out the window. Friendships have been sacrificed on the altar of profit. All human feeling has been suspended. There is only you, the lemon, and the dollar.
So think something a little Cookie Clicker-esque, perhaps, but with more savage disdain for the ruling class and a bit more active involvement on your part. On top of "a genuine supply and demand engine" for your lemonade empire, the game also boasts "a presidential campaign," more than 70 ingredients to experiment with, and "a political opponent who has been watching everything you do." Which is assuredly fine.
This is hitting my fatigue with actual reality and my love of big numbers in all the right ways, folks. I'm pretty eager to get my hands on my competitors and grind them to dust under my boot. Also, to get my hands on some lemons and grind them into lemonade. Do you grind lemons? Probably. Check it out on Steam to find out.

title: Memory is the map in Wane, a roguelike where each biome is a corner of an archaeologist's fading mind
text:
The best art is all about descending into someone's twisted psyche. It doesn't matter who, but the deeper we get into their very being, the better. Now buckle up and prepare for Wane, a roguelike where you quite literally navigate through the deconstructed mind of Declan Wayne, a fading archaeologist.
We just revealed the game at the PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct, and it looks like a corker—for any non-Brits, that means it looks really good. "I used to believe that memory makes a man," says Wayne as he narrates over the gorgeous trailer. "Now I know, it can unmake one, too."
Wishlist Wane on Steam
Release date: TBA
This is the world premiere of Wane, a tactical roguelike where you descend into the depths of a man's memories. It's gorgeous, brutal, and has a demo coming out next year. Wishlist it on Steam .
Wishlist now
That line and the art style were already enough to get me excited for Wane, but then the brass instrumental music swelled and instantly shot this game to the top of my wishlist. It oozes style, and the combat looks pretty hardcore, too.
We see one guy simply do finger guns and magically shoot someone from across the room, and then a woman with a hammer bigger than herself leaps over a railing and does a cinematic slam attack, complete with impact frames. It looks awesome.
These are just two of the six adventurers you can use to form a party of three who must venture into Ravelle, a map of Declan's mind. Each biome is a different section of his psyche, so expect to face off against all of his demons.
This is a roguelike, so expect to die. Between runs, you'll return to Declan's shop, sell goods, and prepare for the next expedition into his mind. You'll probably learn why he's going to all this effort, too.
Wane is being developed by Metis Creative, a tabletop publisher and now videogame studio, too. The trailer reveals little about the world of Wane, but given the history of the devs and the stunning art style already shown, it's a world I already can't wait to learn more about.
There's no release date for the game just yet, but there is a demo coming in 2027. For now you can wishlist Wane on Steam .

title: Beautiful Freaks of the Desert is a speedrunning FPS flipping the middle finger at all things data center
text:
I'm a simple man. I like first-person shooters and making jokes about AI before a combination of data center-enabled climate change and Skynet leads to the end of humanity.
Beautiful Freaks of the Desert then, is poised to make me a very happy man indeed. Beautiful Freaks of the Desert's debut trailer, shown for the first time at the PC Gaming Show, does a great job of showing what the speedrunning FPS is about, using all 50 seconds to showcase intense blasting, striking title cards, and an anti-Data Center sentiment that warms my heart. Give it a watch, the trailer really does have to be seen to be believed.
Wishlist Beautiful Freaks of the Desert on Steam
Release date: Q4, 2026
Beautiful Freaks of the Desert is a world premiere announcement set in a future where competing AI corporations are screwing everyone over. It's fiction, we promise. The speedrunning FPS is reminiscent of Neon White, and will release Q4 2026. Wishlist it on Steam .
Wishlist now
The speedrunning shooter should remind people of Neon White with the clean aesthetic, which channels the golden days of the boomer shooter—a term that's slipped into general usage despite the fact I get at least one angry email every time I use it—and sets it against the backdrop of a seemingly endless war between squabbling technology corporations. There's something charmingly lo-fi about the trailer, which gives me a similar irreverent vibe to the cult classic Cruelty Squad, although this promises to be less of an immersive sim and more a game about jumping around exploded spiders and other enemies with a variety of weaponry.
The game promises 50 bite-sized levels, six different weapon systems, and an open world desert that connects the levels that you can explore on foot or by bike.

title: Escape From Playtime is a co-op survival horror where you play itsy-bitsy toy animals, and its playtest is taking signups now
text:
There is, you must admit, something a bit disconcerting about children's toys. The sightless eyes, the static expressions—it all combines into a hollow unpersonhood that triggers some ancient, primeval fear in the low regions of your brain. Something that also doesn't help: the unslakeable lust for murder.
Alright, that last part maybe does not apply to my childhood teddy bear, but it does apply to the nightmarish denizens of Escape From Playtime, which just announced it's accepting playtest sign-ups at the PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct.
Wishlist Escape From Playtime on Steam
Release date: October 21, 2026
Fancy being scared? Fancy being scared and very, very small? Fancy being scared, very small, and accompanied by up to three of your pals? Escape From Playtime has just the thing for your very specific desires, friend: play as a tiny Smiling Critter navigating a haunted factory in a co-op survival horror whose playtest is taking signups now. Launching October 21 on Steam . You can also sign up for the playtest at EscapeFromPlaytime.com.
Wishlist on Steam
Set in the Poppy Playtime universe—one of those things which is quietly wildly popular—Escape From Playtime bills itself as a 1-4 player co-op survival horror that puts you in the shoes of the setting's Smiling Critters. These are A) haunting and B) probably relatively benign, as inhabitants of this world go. Your goal is to explore an abandoned toy factory at the behest of an ominous voice, who tasks you with finding building materials and other resources with which to do… something really benevolent, probably.
We get a glimpse of the game's creepy puzzle-solving, traversal, and hiding-from-dread-beasts-beyond-comprehension action in the trailer. The Smiling Critters are very small, which means you are even more defenceless than you might have thought possible, and also navigating a lot of environments designed for full-size people as not-full-size animal facsimiles.
It's a whole lot to process, really. You're gonna be making a lot of regrettable decisions about when to split up with your friends, when to hide, when to run, and when to greedily run back to that one room to gather up a resource you missed. This will not end well for you, I think, but I suspect it will be rather enjoyable, if you're the kind of person who enjoys holding their breath in a closet while a murderous beast passes by mere inches away. Who isn't? Find out more on Steam .

title: Young Suns is an optimistic life sim for an unoptimistic time coming in November, and I'm already forming intense opinions about its cast of NPCs
text:
If you had to move to another planet in our solar system, which would you pick? Me, I'd go Neptune. I've always thought it's underrated, as our neighbours go, and it's a particularly pleasing shade of blue. I would die immediately due to cold and pressure, which I guess is a problem.
I guess that problem is why the stars of Young Suns, which just revealed a November 3 release date at the PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct, have elected to set themselves up on Jupiter. They're having a pretty cosy time of it, too: the game is a 1-4 player life sim about building a home for yourself in space, setting up a comforting nook for yourself in a vessel drifting over the face of the newly liberated gas giant.
Wishlist Young Suns on Steam
Release date: November 3, 2026
Imagine a future that's… good? This strange concept is the heart of Young Suns, which tasks you with designing a spaceship home in the stars in orbit around Jupiter, a newly liberated planet with a bright future ahead of it. Build your dreams space-home, explore the environs of our solar system's largest planet, and grow deeply attached to the game's cast of Jupiterians when it hits on November 3. Wishlist it on Steam .
Wishlist now
Jupiter, you see, is a free planet, and it has a whole future ahead of it. It's yours to explore—and your pals' too, if you want. Take your ship, head out to a station, ruin, or what-have-you, and plumb the depths on a hunt for stuff. Then use the stuff you find to help build tomorrow. It's an optimistic game for times that, dare I say it, sometimes feel a little less than optimistic. That's a noble goal, I think.
What we also got a good look at in the PCGS trailer, though, is the people rebuilding Jupiter with you. Whether you bring real-life pals with you or not, the planet's inhabited by a cast of characters who you can get to know in your career.
They'll hand out quests, follow routines and, most importantly, get very excited when you turn up for a chat. No cosy game is complete without a cast of NPCs to grow deeply attached to, and I'm eager to form a set of incredibly vivid and muscular opinions about the denizens of Jupiter.

title: Dust till Dawn is a horror-themed clean-'em-up with music from Silent Hill's composer
text:
At first glance you could be forgiven for thinking Dust till Dawn was a simple cleaning game. Early into the World Premiere trailer, showing the game off for the very first time during the PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct, it seems very mundane at first glance as you clean your way around a Japanese apartment, little cash amounts floating off of each item as you scrub it and put it back in place.
Then, it twists and music from Akira Yamaoka, composer of the Silent Hill games, kicks in and you see the dual nature of Dust till Dawn, which is not just a cleaning game but also a horror, somehow. Don't worry though, you'll still be asked to clean to the best of your ability, even as everything goes to hell around you.
Wishlist Dust till Dawn on Steam
Release date: TBA
Clean houses and get scared in Dust till Dawn, a horror-themed clean-'em-up from Mac n Cheese Games that features music from Akira Yamaoka, the composer of Silent Hill. Wishlist it now on Steam .
Wishlist now
I find eyes unspeakably creepy, despite having several of them tattooed on me, and as a result Dust till Dawn's trailer, which is pretty big on spooky peepers, terrifies me. I'm quite a big fan of the game's aesthetic, which has twisting geometry and early 90s stylings that make it feel like the classic Japanese horror movies of yesteryear. Not that I'll be able to play it, because in addition to being terrified of spooky eyes, I'm also scared of horror games in general, and this looks to be a fairly effective one.
Dust till Dawn comes from Mac n Cheese Games, also developing the "nuns in space" survival horror Void Martyrs. With Dust till Dawn, with an elevator pitch of "Spooky Clean 'Em Up", Mac n Cheese seem to be nailing the one sentence reasons to play its horror games.
If the trailer for Dust till Dawn has whet your appetite, you can wishlist it on Steam here , or check out everything in the PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct on the Steam page . You can also read our roundup article which includes every announcement from the show in the order it aired.

title: Paper co-op deckbuilder Hellcard 2 has a new demo that you can play right now
text:
Hellcard 2, a sequel to the original Hellcard which received 'Very Positive' reviews on Steam, is getting a new co-op demo that you can dive into right now. I'd encourage you to watch the rest of the PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct first, but you could always download the demo while the show goes on.
Hellcard 2 is a co-op roguelite deckbuilder where you descend into dungeons and fight your way through evil minions and dragons made of paper. The paper models give the game an interesting look that makes the deckbuilding aspect feel more tactile and real—the new trailer we just debuted even starts with a scene that looks like a popup book opening.
Download the Hellcard 2 demo on Steam
Release date: 2027
Hellcard 2 is the sequel to the highly praised Hellcard. It's a co-op roguelite deckbuilder with a unique paper aesthetic, and you can download the new demo on Steam .
Wishlist now
You can play Hellcard 2 by yourself or with friends online. If you go solo, don't worry, you'll just control multiple characters simultaneously, so you won't be outgunned by the dragons in the dungeon. If you play with other people, you'll have to coordinate to make sure you're properly utilising all your cards.
One of the more unique mechanics within the genre is that monster placement actually matters. They can either be within melee or ranged distance, so you'll have to decide which cards are best for which threats. Will you go for an all melee deck and let enemies come to you, take them out from afar with a ranged build, or make a mix of the two so you can be ready for any and all situations?
For returning fans of the first Hellcard, what's new in this sequel is the inclusion of gear that your hero can wear. This will not only change their appearance, but also modify your deck and the stats and buffs you get. Let's be real, though, we're all going to pick what looks fashionable over what actually works the best.
If this sounds like your sort of game, download the demo on Steam .

title: Cairn's delayed On the Trail: Deep Water DLC gets a new release date, and you don't have long to wait
text:

title: Core Keeper's Riders of the Underground update drops tomorrow, and you can get a sneak peek of it right here
text:

title: We just saw a big chunk of Thief Remastered gameplay, and I'm more desperate than ever to play
text:
There aren't many things I'm looking forward to more than Nightdive's remaster of the original Thief. Is this because I'm old? Yes, but it's also because Thief is an all-timer videogame and I can't wait to see Nightdive work its magic on it.
At the PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct, we got a hefty helping of gameplay in a new trailer for the remaster, showing Garrett stuffing his pockets in all manner of poorly-lit, erm, manors, plus sewers, crypts, tombs, dungeons—you know, Thief places.
Wishlist Thief: The Dark Project Remastered on Steam
Release date: TBA
Get ready to stuff your pockets because Nightdive's Thief remaster looks downright glorious in a new, gameplay-heavy trailer. We even got a peek at the controller UI, which looks to be taking its cues from the original game's mod scene. Good choice. There's no release date just yet, so make sure you wishlist it on Steam to keep up with the news.
Wishlist now
It looks great. I've said it before and I'll say it again: Nightdive has gotten 'making games look how you remember them looking' down to an art. No ugly uprezzed textures or weirdly 3D models, just a lot of deft touches that keep the game's original art style intact.
I'm also pretty sure we got a glimpse of the game's controller support, and it looks like the remaster is taking its cues from the (very good) already-existing controller mods for the un-remastered version of the game.
You can select items using a handy-dandy inventory wheel, which is just how the mods do it. Supposing Nightdive is taking its cues from them, then I imagine we're going to get something that feels almost weirdly well-suited to a PC game originally released in 1998. The mods make flicking between your various arrow types (remember to stock up on water and moss, hard-mode players) very easy indeed—I imagine Nightdive's version might make it even easier.
I'll say this, though: this trailer, with its driving soundtrack and ample blackjacking and arrow-loosing, doesn't quite match my memories of Thief, which mostly consist of a lot of standing in dark corners and memorising guard patrol routes. Where's the 10-hour 'Hanging out with Garrett behind a door' ASMR YouTube video, Nightdive? You're missing a trick there.

title: Defend your farm from a gaze of raccoons in this charming tower defense roguelite, out tomorrow
text:
Never say I'm biased or I don't have an open mind, because here I am, telling you about a videogame where raccoons—my favourite animal on this Earth—are the enemy. Heartbreaking, I know. In The Rabbit Haul, the crafty little scamps are pestering a bunny named Sprout, so they decide to turn their garden into a warzone that can keep the mischievous Trash Panda Posse at bay.
Why does Sprout need to keep the raccoons away? Well, they kind of destroyed the town. I'm sure they didn't mean to and were just looking for snacks. Still, one has to defend one's home, so Sprout gets to planting deadly organic weaponry during the day and fighting off the hordes of ringtails at night. Sprout gets in on the action themselves, so you won't just be passively watching your plants do all the hard work.

The Rabbit Haul feels a bit like plants versus raccoons, only instead of pure tower defense, you actually have to tend to your garden to grow your organic weaponry. You prepare the flora in a grid, and can choose to either overwhelm your foes with unimaginable force or try to outsmart them with clever plant synergies. You'll have to improvise, adapt, and overcome, because the waves of raccoons get stronger each night, and if they're successful, they'll trash your garden and steal away your resources.
The Rabbit Haul is a roguelite, so you'll be rebuilding Sprout's town between runs. Restore shops, fix up homes, and welcome new characters into the cosy little hamlet, and unlock upgrades that'll help you in future attempts. And no farming sim would be complete without some dress up options, so rest assured, you can put Sprout in lots of adorable little outfits.
Revealed for the first time at the PC Gaming Show were new features, such as a snowy biome, what looks to be a pirate raccoon enemy type—again, why must this game make me fight the things I love—more characters and plant towers, and even an infinite mode. title: Virtue and a Sledgehammer announces October 27 release date with another banger of a trailer
text:
"A machine will never hate itself enough to become better." That's the unbelievably metal quote we just saw in the latest Virtue and a Sledgehammer trailer, revealed on the PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct alongside the game's launch date: October 27.
We showed off some of the hammer-wielding action in our June show , so we already knew this was going to be a bizarre descent into the human psyche, as well as a game about smashing robots to bits. I love destructible environments, and I'm getting serious Red Faction: Guerrilla vibes from the carnage on offer here. What's more, these new words tell us a lot about developer Selkie Harbour's and Deconstructeam's views on self-improvement: it is fuelled by hatred, not love.
Wishlist Virtue and a Sledgehammer on Steam
Release date: October 27, 2026
Return to your hometown and destroy it brick by brick, all while smashing through androids that have digitised your once-neighbours. Wishlist it on Steam .
Wishlist now
In hindsight, that's pretty obvious when you consider the premise of Virtue and a Sledgehammer. You're returning to your hometown and tearing it down brick by brick, all while smashing through the androids that have digitised your once-neighbours.
There's something therapeutic going on too, though. In the last trailer we aired, we see flashbacks of moments from our protagonist's life. Visiting a grave, hanging out with friends in the woods, strangling a woman in the woods. Add to that the therapy-esque questions that get more and more deranged as the trailer goes on, and there's clearly a lot to unpack here.
I love videogames that offer deep, emotionally nuanced storytelling. I also adore ones where you can relish in the act of playing, either through sheer destruction or systems that let you interact with the world in creative ways. Virtue and a Sledgehammer is doing both. October 27 can't come soon enough.
If you also can't wait, head over to Steam and check out Virtue and a Sledgehammer's demo or wishlist the game ahead of launch. Get a feel for that sweet, sweet, stylish sledgehammer-swinging action.

Each world you arrive on has a mission for you to complete. These can range from simple objectives like clearing an area of enemies, or more complex ones like building railguns to shoot down space ships. title: Marked For Mayhem is a 4-player dungeon crawler that wants you to try to win as a team while also beating all your teammates as a player—good luck
text:
Heads up, hotshot: you are being dispatched to a hostile alien planet. You will have to overcome life-or-death challenges that test your wits, physicality, and raw luck. You may die. You will almost certainly be hurt. Also, the whole thing is being televised. How many friends would you like to take with you?
If you answered three, you're in luck—Marked For Mayhem is a four-player dungeon crawler which just got a world premiere at the PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct, and I pretty much just gave you its elevator pitch in the opening paragraph. The aim of the game is to venture to planets that would really quite like to kill you and complete bounties, beat foes, take on bosses, and even partake in a few minigames.
Wishlist Marked for Mayhem on Steam
Release date: TBA
Marked For Mayhem is a four-player dungeon crawler with an interesting premise: what if you had to deal with two essentially contradictory goals at once? Here, it means working with your team to overcome challenges while also competing with your teammates for the singular, individual winner position. I predict broken friendships aplenty. Sign up for the beta .
Wishlist now
To do that, you'll need to cooperate with your pals. But this is no love-in: you're competing with them too. In addition to trying to beat missions as a team, you're all competing individually to see who can nab the highest score. And if that ain't a dose of tension that will absolutely, definitely result in a few teams biffing their missions in a fit of competitive pique, I don't know what is.
We get a little of this in the trailer, where we see teams of competitors uniting to take on big robotic bosses, taking on hordes of foes in spacious arenas, and navigating environmental hazards. But they're collecting points all for themselves, too, and at the end just one of them gets to take centre stage as the singular winner.
It's an interesting wrinkle, ain't it? I rather like the idea of compelling players to deal with two contradictory impulses at once—to function as a team and to win as an individual. I'll be honest, it's the kind of thing that might lead to me and my pals not speaking to one another for months. But so long as I win, well, it's all worth it.

title: I lost hours to this roguelike card-based city builder even though I had no idea how all of those words could fit together
text:
When I first heard about this card-based roguelike city builder, I was confused. Then I played a round. And another. And another. And another. And before I knew it far too much time had passed and I was absolutely hooked. That game is Toxic Frontier, and we just revealed it at the PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct.
Toxic Frontier plays on a hexagonal grid that makes it feel a bit like Settlers of Catan, only I'm not screaming at my housemates because they won't accept my very reasonable trade offers. You draw cards such as villages, forests, sheep, mountains, lakes, and more, and try to find the synergies while expanding into the titular toxic wasteland.
Wishlist Toxic Frontier on Steam
Release date: TBA
Rebuild amongst the fog and ruin of a radioactive wasteland in Toxic Frontier. It doesn't have a release date yet, so wishlist it on Steam to stay up-to-date with all the news.
Wishlist now
You don't combine cards just by stacking them on top of each other. Some you do, but it often gets more complicated than that. Surround a village with other villages, for example, and the central one becomes a town. Repeat the process and you get a city.
That process is hampered by the terrain you discover as you slowly push back the fog. By building up your settlements and expanding the land, you'll push deeper into the toxic mists, often unearthing nasty horrors like wandering mutants that will raid your lumberjack homes, or polluted wastelands that have to be cleansed.
But where does the roguelike element come into it? Well, each level has a semi-randomised set of objectives and you only have a limited number of cards to complete them. Each card you place also rewards you with points that you need to unlock more cards. Bigger and more complex combos give more points, so you've got to experiment and try to make the most out of what you've got.
I learned the hard way that not all the combos are easy to do, so expect to lose a lot when the game comes out. When that is, we don't know. For now, all you can do is wishlist Toxic Frontier on Steam .

text:
Modder Doneda has released a particularly funky and exciting mod for Elden Ring Nightreign, porting Dark Souls 2's Frozen Eleum Loyce and Frigid Outskirts as a standalone map. They also have a trailer up for the project on YouTube. Doneda's a bit of a Dark Souls 2 expert⁠—they previously restored the remains of a cut sewers map to the sequel for demonstration purposes.
Gun to my head, I think the Brume Tower is my favorite DS2 level, but Eleum Loyce still feels like a dear old friend. I enjoyed base DS2 more than most, but the Lost Crowns DLCs were on a whole different level. Other FromSoft DLCs may be better in a vacuum (Old Hunters, Shadow of the Erdtree), but there has never been a more staggering, exhilarating leap in quality between one of the studio's games and its corresponding expansion.
While Brume Tower may be my beautiful baby, it just wouldn't fit in Nightreign like Eleum Loyce does: The wide open Outskirts and walled city can mimic the mini open world of Limveld in a way the twisty, narrow Brume Tower couldn't manage. My favorite detail is that it looks like the night two circle narrows down on the underground chaos arena where you fight the Burnt Ivory King , a fun and creative recontextualizing of the level's original flow.
Doneda's new map is already available for download on the Nightreign Nexus. You'll need to install Mod Engine 3 beforehand to run it⁠—most, if not all Nightreign mods require the utility. Doneda seems intent on making more modded Nightreign maps, and you can follow their work on YouTube or support them via Ko-fi .
You talk about love/hate relationships, I'd say I have a ⅔ hate, ⅓ love relationship with Nightreign. Its Deep of Night update gave me and my friends incentive to keep playing, while it introduces some truly incredible boss fights⁠—stuff like The Balancers and Libra give me hope that FromSoft can still surprise, delight, and challenge in a post-Promised Consort world.
But Deep of Night also subjected us to the most frustrating, artless version of FromSoftware difficulty I've yet seen, and the studio appears to have quietly stopped supporting the game to work on The Duskbloods⁠—and hopefully something else, too?
Perhaps I should take the glass half full view of FromSoft releasing a multiplayer game, supporting it a bit, but not feeling compelled to turn it into a forever empire of live service returns. In the absence of official support, though, there have been some weird, exciting things happening with Nightreign. Yui's Nightreign iteration of her signature Seamless Co-op mod is a welcome addition for more "chill with your friends" -style play, while I've been intrigued by gameplay videos of TerraMag's SotE and ds3 weapons , a "no duh" addition that I'm still surprised FromSoft didn't manage itself.

title: First 5-day Tokyo Game Show in 30 years cuts back to 4 in face of Typhoon Dujuan
text:
As reported by Kotaku , the organizers of the Tokyo Game Show have announced that its final day has been canceled and tickets for Monday, September 21 will be refunded. This was supposed to be the first five-day event in TGS' 30-year run⁠—while I am not a superstitious man, God or karma or something may be trying to tell us that it's just supposed to be a four-day deal.
"Due to the approach of Typhoon No. 25, strong winds and rain are expected to intensify in the afternoon and beyond, and disruptions to transportation are also a concern," event organizers wrote on Twitter . "Therefore, prioritizing the safety of all attendees, exhibitors, and related parties, as well as ensuring safe return home, we have decided to cancel the event for the entire day."

The TGS showfloor will remain open for today, September 20, with potential modifications. There is no word on how the event will address publishers and devs who rented out space for the final day.
As reported by the Japan Times , Dujuan is the 25th named typhoon of 2026, and is predicted to dump the heaviest rainfall (almost 16 inches) on the Kanto region containing Tokyo. Nippon Airways has canceled many flights in the region, while the East Japan Railway is fully and partially suspending service on some lines.
We were on the ground at TGS 2026 as part of our annual PC Gaming Show: Tokyo Direct, interviewing developers and showcasing trailers for a number of upcoming games. title: Steam Week in Review: This indie publisher released 29 terrible-looking Steam games in a single day—will they make any money?
text:
It's been a busy week for prodigious game publisher Hard Shark Games: on September 15 it released an astonishing 29 games on Steam across a huge variety of genres.
Not only did Hard Shark Games publish that many games, but the company is also marked as developer for every one of them. All of which, mind you, are early access affairs. "We're launching in Early Access to involve the community from the very start," reads the first sentence of every single one of the early access blurbs for Hard Shark Games released in September 2026, which include genres as diverse as racing, retail sim, survival horror, sport, flight sim and 2D platformer.
The same is true for some of the 29 games Hard Shark Games released on March 4 last year: "We're launching in Early Access to involve the community from the very start," reads the first line in the blurb for Speedboat Simulator . “We're launching in Early Access to involve the community from the very start," reads the first line in the blurb for Toy Battlegrounds: Shoot 'Em Up Survival . You get the idea.
(Image credit: Hard Shark Games) The "company" has also taken a similar approach to early access updates: the update notes for Starship Fighters , Sky Combat and Streets of Rageness (!) are identical: "Optimized several core systems, resulting in smoother gameplay and up to 10% better overall performance, especially during longer sessions," reads the first sentence of all three, each of which were published on March 5 within five minutes of each other.
Will Hard Shark Games profit from any of the 29 Steam games it released last week? You may be surprised. It costs $100 to open a Steam store page, which is recoupable if a game makes more than $1,000 adjusted gross revenue. So it would have cost Hard Shark Games $2,900 to publish its 29 very unpromising looking games on Steam, all of which carry an AI disclosure for capsule art but no other aspect of development.
Using the popular Boxleiter Method (via impress.games ), which uses a game's public Steam review count to estimate sales, Supermarket Life Simulator—to use just one example—could have made as much as $885 as a high estimate, or $295 on the lower end. Then there's Pool: it could have made as much as $2,780 or as little as $926. Meanwhile, for F1 Simulator we're looking at $1,686 as a high estimate and $562 as a low.
(Image credit: Hard Shark Games) So adding up the low estimates, those three games alone—of 29—have made $1,783 in the five days since release. That's well over half of Hard Shark Games' outlay for the store listings in less than a week on the market, though if the high estimates are more accurate, the $2,900 outlay has been long passed and Hard Shark Games' investment is already paying off handsomely.
Of course, that assumes these games cost nothing to make, and that's unlikely, even though they all look pretty low effort. For example, Supermarket Life Simulator clearly uses the $50 Checkout Frenzy - Convenience Store Simulator Unity template, which very many retail sims on Steam do. There's nothing wrong with using a template, but comparing the images of Supermarket Life Simulator with the Unity template screenshots reveals some identical grocery imagery. Steam user reviews claim Supermarket Life Simulator is a straight asset flip of the template, and this is an accusation levelled at Hard Shark Games quite often .
(Also: how the heck did Kratos end up in a screenshot for the creative-titled Axe Slasher ?)
Hard Shark Games has a total of 217 listings on Steam. Of all of those—which take in 121 games and 96 demos—the highest peak concurrent player figure is a whopping 13. To add insult to injury, that record high is for a demo , namely Supermarket Simulator Pro Demo, which is no longer available. So not many people play these games in the scheme of things, but assuming Hard Shark Games is just one person turning out extremely cheap template-based software at a rapid pace, the enterprise is definitely capable of making a tidy sum of money.
I've reached out to Hard Shark Games to see if someone there will shed further light on their method. It's hardly the least prolific publisher on Steam though: BFG Entertainment has released a whopping 555 games, while PlayWay—the spiritual home of quickly turned around retail sims—has 340.

Last week's Steam deep cuts
(Image credit: SonderingEmily)
Lily's World XD | September 18
Following in the footsteps of fake desktop games like Hypnospace Outlaw and Emily is Away, Lily's World XD takes place in an antiquated 2004 operating system. An ancient laptop is found in a skip bin and, naturally, its contents are cause for much alarm. Via clues in Lily's message history and blog a disturbing mystery unfolds amid the digital nostalgia. Expect the fourth wall to be broken.
20 More, Somehow Even Smaller, Mazes | September 18
The name says it all really: there are 20 maze-oriented puzzles here. "More", because it's a follow-up to 20 Small Mazes , which released in 2024 and has since amassed over 6,500 "overwhelmingly positive" reviews. It's a short 'n' sweet affair that you'll be able to wrap up in around 30 minutes, assuming your brain isn't too rotted. Best of all: it's free.
BRAZILIAN DRUG DEALER BEFORE 4: DEMONS FROM THE PORTAL TO HELL I OPENED ARE STILL IN THE FAVELA AND NOW I HAVE TO SAVE MAMADAS FROM RONALDO | September 16
The latest in this series of excessively titled boomer shooters is actually a standalone expansion to Brazilian Drug Dealer 3 (whose subtitle I will not include here because it's even longer than the above). These are enormously fun and over the top run and gunners made in the original Quake engine, but with dashing and double jumping. Come for the deliberately garish presentation, stay for the rich Brazilian vibes (maybe).
Dimraeth | September 16
This early access cooperative ARPG has absolutely stunning pixel art recalling the ye olde Mana JRPGs. In practice it plays a bit more like a souls-like spin Diablo: there are eight races and six classes planned, which can be mixed and matched towards 48 "distinct" archetypes. Combat isn't about relentless clicking: you can't just spam attacks. The early access period is expected to last between 18 and 24 months.

title: Silent Hill: Townfall review
text:
Need to know
What is it? A single-player psychological horror game which takes place on an isolated Scottish island. The protagonist Simon Ordell has to solve puzzles, fight monsters, and figure out what the hell is going on.
Release date September 24, 2026
Expect to pay $50 / £45
Developer Screen Burn
Publisher Konami
Reviewed on RTX 3070, Core AMD Ryzen 5 5600G, 16GB RAM
Multiplayer No
Steam Deck Unknown
Link Steam
Walking up to the old town of St Amelia for the first time in Silent Hill: Townfall, I was greeted by that familiar thick fog and eerie quiet—an omen of the horrors to come. I know what kind of monsters are waiting for me beyond the fog and I am painfully aware of just how unprepared I am for it—with no flashlight, healing items, or weapon on hand. But weirdly enough none of that matters, because for the first time in a Silent Hill game I feel content.
St Amelia is a fictional town, but as I'm sure many players based in the UK will soon discover, developer Screen Burn breathes so much life into this sleepy fishing village that I could've sworn I'd been here before. It's certainly a strange feeling to have in a game like this, but with Konami opening Silent Hill up to the world it's now the UK's turn to have our sense of home toyed with.
Here to suffer
(Image credit: Konami) The story follows Simon Ordell, a man unknown to us and himself. The only sense of person he has comes from a medical bracelet with his name, date of birth, and blood type written on it. I watched as he dragged himself up from the waves of the North Sea, onto the docks, and headed into St Amelia seeking help and answers as to why he's here on this cold foggy island.
A Silent Hill game is nothing without its setting and St Amelia delivers. I spent more time than I'd care to admit reading info boards about the history of fishing on the island and peeping over fences to see how the locals had done up their gardens. The more I explored, the better sense I got of the kind of people who lived in this town and what had happened to them.
Simon also sees more than just the old town as he ventures to a hospital, a corporate office, your classic Silent Hill supernatural 'other place', and, brace yourself, some new builds. My time in St Amelia flew by rather quickly, with just 13 hours spent in total, but that was more than enough to be rewarded with heaps of brilliant visual storytelling and the usual gift of stressful encounters.
Konami Konami Konami St Amelia has its fair share of gut-wrenching horrors lurking around each corner, though—you don't spend a grand total of 35 minutes and five seconds hiding in lockers unless there's something pretty bad waiting for you on the other side. But even still, I found myself drawn to exploring the fog because my curiosity outweighed my fear.
But the further I progressed the less content I became. Not because there were more faceless and bound monsters stumbling around (although that didn't help), but because there was more to the island than St Amelia's historic old town. There was a side that was painfully familiar—cobblestone streets shifted into tarmac roads and cottages were turned into flats for better efficiency. The island changed as Simon moved away from the heart of St Amelia and towards the parasite which had latched onto it.
The town itself felt alive more than just lived in, and if that doesn't tick all the boxes for a world-class Silent Hill setting, I don't know what does.
Try to B positive
(Image credit: Konami) A good rule of thumb in Silent Hill is to approach its puzzles with lateral thinking, and Townfall is no different. They start fairly easy, coaching you in the art of taking in absolutely everything from your surroundings, digesting it, and then stitching together an answer from what has been gathered. It's the classic case of finding the combination to a lock by sifting through letters conveniently left scattered around the near vicinity.
But as I spent more time in St Amelia, my brain gradually got the hang of looking at things from a Silent Hill perspective. And although the puzzles got harder it didn't feel like a noticeable difference. Hell, the first thing I thought when stumbling across a bunch of blood types scribbled across the wall was "This is a puzzle and it wants me to figure out how to create blood type A+". If it weren't for the 7+ hours I'd already spent in Townfall I doubt that would have been my default response.
There were a few exceptions towards the very end of the game, however, I think a fresh brain would have had far less issues. Take the dreaded pipe room for example, where I had to use what looked to be morse code to twist a room full of levers in the right direction. After bashing my head against my desk my synapses sparked, a thought was formed, and I figured it out—I wish you all the best of luck with that one.
(Image credit: Konami) The puzzles aren't the only smart design features in Townfall, though, with the best and brightest being the handheld CRTV. This quickly became my closest companion as it allowed me to see the creepies through any wall or obstacle. It may seem like a bit of a cheat code getting to know where the monsters are but there are some limitations.
The CRTV may be the most creative, fun, and useful puzzle solving tool I've ever had the pleasure of playing with.
It's not always crystal clear where the monsters were, sometimes the CRTV could be a smidge off or it wouldn't relay that a monster is actually further away than it first seemed. It also can't show multiple enemies on one frequency, which means I had to toggle between several to see all the monsters that were close.
I wouldn't say I'm much of a pacifist but I opted to forgo the planks of wood, pipes, and firearms for most of the game, instead favouring the CRTV as my weapon against the monsters to help me stealth around them. I played on the normal difficulty and I didn't have a run in with a monster until quite far into the latter stages of the game. They're not blind, I was just able to move around them with some ease if I used the CRTV correctly and was cautiously optimistic about how fast Simon could run.
Even with all its finicky buttons the CRTV may be the most creative, fun, and useful puzzle solving tool I've ever had the pleasure of playing with. It turned navigating Townfall into one big scary puzzle, which is exactly what I look for in Silent Hill.
You can't change
(Image credit: Konami) But all of these amazing puzzles and fantastic world building would be for nought if Townfall hadn't also been able to pull off the kind of beautiful and psychologically jarring storytelling we've come to expect from the Silent Hill series.
But the fact that there's something off about Simon isn't what interests me—the fun part is finding out what he did.
To say there's something wrong with Simon would be to state the obvious. We're in a Silent Hill game after all, and no one in their sound mind would hallucinate grotesque faceless monsters which shoot needles out from their abdomens. But the fact that there's something off about Simon isn't what interests me—the fun part is finding out what he did to end up like this. It's clear that people in the town are angry, that some awful disaster happened on this island which rocked its community to its core. What's unclear, however, is why it involves some seemingly random American dude with induced amnesia.
But Simon's not on his own. There are two other characters who also inhabit this liminal space with him—Zoe and Richard. At first I just thought these to be your typical filler characters but as it turns out these two are perhaps the most interesting characters to have ever fallen into the fog.
Zoe and Richard portray different sides of the same disaster that Simon's caught in the middle of, with one being wrongfully guilty and the other willfully ignorant. Both have their own playable segments within the game in which their characters are explored in depth alongside the roles they played in the catastrophe, and through this I began to piece together Simon's story.
(Image credit: Konami) My favourite sequence in all of Townfall was actually Zoe's part. In this she relives the aftermath of the disaster as a nurse and a first responder to the victims as she tries to save the life of an unknown patient.
I am not a trained nurse so taking the patient's readings, running tests, and ultimately medicating them was probably one of the more stressful experiences I've had in a horror game. But it was worth it because through the stress I understood her guilt and trauma with painful clarity. It also made it clear why she's found herself wrapped up in this mess.
Then there's Richard who is an opposite to Zoe in every sense of the word. He's not blameless or caring; he's an asshole. But boy, is he an interesting character study. I won't go into too much detail concerning Richard as his story is one that is better experienced firsthand. But, like with Zoe, after playing through his sequence it became clear to me what this game's curse is. While the answer seemed simple at first examining the curse through the lens of three different characters adds enough diversity for an incredibly rewarding story and analysis of its characters.
Konami My only issue with Townfall was that I didn't get to spend more time with Zoe and Richard, because in comparison Simon is just a little boring. His role as a blank template for players to print themselves onto worked wonders for immersion but ultimately his character suffered for it. I found myself drawn more to Zoe and Richard, two characters who had more invested in this community from the get go.
That's not to say I dislike Simon. He's a fantastic character who comes into his own during the latter stages of the story and is someone who will grow on me the more time I spend mulling Townfall over.
After all was said and done and I'd finally reached the end of Townfall's brilliant story, my overwhelming feeling was one of relief. Like Silent Hill f before it, Townfall had some monumental expectations to live up to and the unenviable task of proving that yet again the mystique of Silent Hill is not limited to one mountainous town. But it's now clear that Screen Burn absolutely understands what makes a great Silent Hill game and the series is better off for it.

title: WoW devs surprised to find pure liquid nostalgia is popular
text:
World of Warcraft: Forever 's beta has been utterly rammed with server issues —issues that I'm pleased to say were fixed in relatively short order, and one I certainly don't resent anybody for. What does jump my eyebrows up my head is the fact that its developers are shocked that the game's popular.
For those not in the know, Forever's essentially Classic+. A version of the game as it was back in 2004, but with a bunch of changes made not to modernise it, but to make that old school vision better. Over 1,000 extra quests, new zones, redesigned talented trees, new racial abilities, and some major improvements to lighting.
It's pure, distilled liquid nostalgia. A fat, juicy worm for shmucks (like me) to chomp onto and be shocked when there's a hook in our mouth—a fact that apparently completely disarmed the beta's development team: "AHMAGERD, this game is 20 years old, how do you still suck at this!?!" Rhetorically asks Tom Ellis, senior game producer, on X :
"Heh, fair enough, short answer is, this is our BETA PTR environment stack, it's not a production stack by a long, long, long, long, long, long shot. Betas for WoW aren't usually huge meter movers so this environment just isn't that powerful. This led to the first problem you saw today."
(Image credit: Blizzard) From the dev's end, nothing was amiss when players were being booted out after a long queue time: "We were hitting the BGS metering system that protects their services from falling over under extreme load. Our tiny little REGIONAL [server] with its two connections that were trying to login A LOT of users, even though it was nowhere near capped on CPU, was completely screwing the math that system was using. We scaled that 2 to an 8 and immediately the flood gates opened once again."
Ellis adds that this is completely unprecedented: "First time anyone's seen it kick in when there wasn't an obvious CPU issue to go along with it. 20 years, always something new."
You can read the full post for the technical mumbo jumbo, but the point is, it's all working better now: "Right now things are incredibly smooth for the first few hours of a public beta, Classic teams watching and fixing anything blocking that comes up but we're otherwise pretty much done for the night, enjoy!"
Josh Greenfield, also a senior game designer, commented : "The craziest numbers I've seen in 17 years working at Blizzard and almost eight years on classic. We've got something really special here."
And you know what, I'm inclined to agree. Forever has me in a chokehold. I've both had rose-tinted goggles forcibly drilled into my face, and I've been genuinely impressed by the changes made already. Forever crawled out of an alternate universe where the modern MMO was never invented, and all the inconvenience and friction of the past was conserved, but not entirely left to burn you.

title: I tried to make a jpg bigger than mathematically possible out of an entire year's worth of PC Gamer magazine pages
text:
We recently had a full archive of PC Gamer magazines digitised for us, covering the very inception of our illustrious 33 year-old publication right up to 2008. Some lucky human had to dig into the archive in the regularly flooded basement of PC Gamer towers and scan each and every page.
I've been noodling around with different ways to use these funky little assets of ours in interesting ways, and Jacob suggested why not use them to create photo mosaics, with the individual pages working effectively as pixels for an image.
So, that's exactly what I am presenting to you here, below. This is at over 6000% zoom into the overall image, and it will go up to 11000% zoom but the resolution in the individual jpgs break down zoomed that tightly in. Still, start slowly zooming out and let me know how quickly you guess what the overall image is, I would definitely recommend hitting the fullscreen button, btw. The year was 2004, if you want a hint.
Zoom out and see how quickly you guess the image
So, how quickly did you guess? Of course I picked the year 2004 specifically, and this image is built from every issue of PC Gamer, including specials, to build out the full picture.
I should get out of the way right up front that this is not an AI generated image. Though I did use Google's AI Studio to help me create a Python script to analyse the original image using Pillow (PIL) and then manage, crop, and rasterise using pypdfium2. That script then uses further libraries to run colour matching and image stitching to create the final mosaic to match the target image, again using PIL and also numpy.
So the actual process of parsing the pages and creating the image is all done via a Python script, on my home PC, with no AI processing baked in.
I have also used AI Studio to help get the viewer above to actually embed on the site, because I don't think anyone would thank me for dropping an 800 MB image onto this page for you guys to wait to render. It primarily relies on the open-source OpenSeadragon viewer to access the image and provide the fully zoomable experience, with the Deep Zoom (DZI) API doing the pyramid rendering grunt work.
And I learned a lot in the process. Primarily that there are very specific mathematical limits to how big a jpg you can create. I learned that the hard way by trying to create an image that exceeded the absolute mathematical limits of the jpg standard. The hard jpg limit is 65,535 px and I had was trying to get the Python script to generate an 81,920 x 109,568 image.
So, I had to scale back my ambitions.
There's no such limit to pngs, however, so I could potentially flip to that file format, but I fear straying into multi-gigabtyte sized image files. Though at least you'd be able to read the actual magazine pages more easily.
I also discovered a way to absolutely max out the 64 GB memory capacity of my home PC, too. The python script that runs through the whole mosaic creation process slams the memory, to the point where at times it was chowing down on 52 GB of the expensive stuff. I was watching on Task Manager in case it did bad things, and the system as a whole slowed to a crawl at points.
Let me know in the comments if there are other PC Gaming classics you would like to see rendered using the pages of this fine publication, and I'll put some more together.

title: Full unicorn vomit, or stealthed-out mean machine? I want to know how much RGB festoons your gaming PC, please and thank you
text:
Take a look at most modern PC gaming setups, and you'll find some RGB lighting somewhere. Blazing LEDs and PC gaming have gone hand in hand for what feels like generations now, but I want to know where you stand—are you down with the RGB clown, or does the whole neon-lit endeavour make your stomach turn?
Or perhaps your preferences sit somewhere in between? Whatever the case, I'd be grateful if you'd answer the poll below and tell me how much RGB currently festoons your personal PC gaming setup.
Did I miss something? There's no accounting for taste, as the old saying goes, so feel free to tell me in the comments what particular flavour of arr-gee-bee setup you're running. If any at all, of course.
Personally, I like a good dose of solid-colour lighting to bathe me in neon while I game, but I'm not sold on the full unicorn vomit rainbow display. My first port of call when testing an RGB-lit gaming keyboard is normally the lighting section of the software, as most of the models I test are set to some sort of eye-searing wave pattern straight from the box.
And there are enough distractions in modern life without my peripherals winking at me all day long. The exception, however, is my Corsair Vengeance RGB DDR5 kit, which has been softly glowing in rainbow tones since the day I first installed it three years ago.
Future Future Occasionally I stare at those modules, nestled in my otherwise all-red PC, and wonder whether I should change the settings. Yet they've been there long enough to be oddly comforting, creating a dash of contrast in what otherwise might be a rather dull, one-colour lighting setup.
And now I look at the photos, I've realised the topside of my graphics card is pumping a little bit of extra colour into the whole affair. I sit next to this rig all day long and I've never really noticed.
Perhaps I find a bit of rainbow RGB soothing after all? Anyway, the question is this: Full RGB, not for me, or something in between? Get thee to the polling booth, PC gamers. Please and thank you, and all that.

title: Steam Frame's odd charging behaviour gets patched: cuts recharge times in half in some instances
text:
A new version of SteamOS for Steam Frame has just landed. The company has fixed a few issues with the VR headset following its launch last week, which I'll get to in a bit, but one change stood out to me in the patch notes: Valve has added "substantially faster charging while unit is off / sleeping."
I found the Steam Frame to be slow to charge during my time testing it ahead of my review. It took over two hours to go from totally depleted to fully charged (you can see the full timings in the battery section of my Steam Frame review ). When I installed a power meter between the charger and the outlet, it read just 11 W, which is much lower than the maximum output that could be delivered by the official power adapter, which is 45 W.
So, I reached out to Valve with my findings. Mostly to see if this was some sort of protection measure for the battery's long-term health.
Valve responded: "An empty battery takes around two hours to charge to full capacity. However, the charging is not linear. There is fast charging from 0 to 65%, and regular charging from 65% and up. Charging to 65% is expected to take less than 40 minutes. (Note: these values may be optimized over time, and are therefore subject to change.)"
I hadn't noticed any fast charging myself—it was always 11 W or thereabouts on my power meter throughout a full charge cycle—so this led to further experimentation. It might seem normal for most users, but when you're actively trying to test charging times, you tend to let the device run flat first. This time I didn't.
(Image credit: Future) I ran the battery on the Frame down to around 4%, then started charging it. Lo and behold, the power meter read roughly 31 W, and the Steam Frame went from 4% to 65% in 35 minutes. Valve's timing was pretty spot-on. After that, it dropped to 18 W for the final charge to 100%, with a total charge time of just 75 minutes.
I thought I was doing the right thing by leaving the Frame switched off during charging to save power and charge it faster. Turns out, I was doing the exact opposite, and I'm sure others would've fallen foul of this too once the headset was in the hands of thousands of customers.
(Image credit: Future) Thankfully, this is one of the first things to be addressed in the latest version of SteamOS for Steam Frame, version 0.3.0 . I've had a quick test with the update installed, and my power meter now reads 27 W with the Frame switched off. That's much higher.
This makes way more sense to me; I can now enjoy the headset until the final juice leaves the cell, and not have to worry about needlessly doubling the charging time in doing so.
Here are the other changes in the update:
General
Substantially faster charging while unit is off / sleeping
Improved controller tracking while haptics are active
Improved system stability and reliability under high load
Fixed "garbled audio" microphone bug
UX
Fixed per-app Motion Smoothing -> "Force Always-On" setting (was getting ignored)
Improved motion smoothing behavior in Alyx
Added VR Settings control for "Game dimming when dashboard is visible"
VR Settings -> Play Area no longer auto-shows bounds
Developer
Change Playable performance criteria to allow any resolution (was: 1440p)
Vulkan layer fixes for increased game compatibility
Multiple improvements to overall system / OS performance
Multiple improvements to graphics performance (Mesa)
Valve is still building out the library of games that are officially certified to run on Steam Frame via Proton and FEX layers, but it looks like that's one area of focus for the company as units start to arrive with customers.
Did you get a Steam Frame reservation? You can do your bit and help shape our understanding of availability by logging your answer on this community website .

title: I remember when Jensen Huang used to sell me GPUs, now he's out there having to deny that AI will cause 'the end of the world'
text:
The hardware landscape of 2021 feels like a distant world. Case in point this past week, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said that talk of an AI-induced extinction event for humanity is overblown and "not grounded in science." Huang's comments were in part responding to claims made earlier this month by ex-Anthropic researcher, Jacob Coxon, saying that AI progress 'could kill us all by the end of the decade' .
"2030 is not going to be the end of the world. There is 0% chance that's going to be the end of the world," Huang told CBS News on Friday . "Scaring people is unnecessary. It is irresponsible."
Compare and contrast this state of affairs to five years ago, when the keynote for GTC 2021 came to you predominantly from Huang's own kitchen , and the month before Nvidia spent a decent chunk of change on a tiny leather jacket emoji to poke fun at its CEO . Ah, simpler times; the leather jackets persist, but now Huang is fielding calls on-stage from the US president, offering assurances to Trump that he "saw through" all of the AI doomsaying .
As I've said before, I barely remember the last time Nvidia mentioned gaming at all in an earnings call , with the company being all-in on AI for some time now. As such, Huang told CBS News last week, "Our company's success is directly connected to the safe deployment of [AI] products and services. If we don't continue to do that, our value would be diminished."
Still, it's a strange state of affairs when the guy who used to primarily sell us PC gamers GPUs is having to offer assurances that the world isn't ending. That's all without saying anything about the CEO rocking up to the White House in a leather jacket and joining the US president on his expedition to convince China to 'open up' .
Mind you, the more things change, the more they stay the same, as one of our Dave's big questions for Nvidia back in 2021 was 'Can Nvidia actually build enough GPUs to please gamers?' Obviously, the reasons for GPU scarcity are different now , but it remains a mission to track down a 50-series GPU at MSRP .

title: WoW: Forever mentally broke me with a boulder
text:
WoW Forever is basically my first time experiencing Blizzard's MMO for a significant amount of time—that level 13 Paladin rotting away on my retail account for the last eight years doesn't count—and you know what? Even as someone who isn't rocking around Azeroth in rose-tinted glasses, I'm having a pretty sweet time.
I even surprised myself by how endeared I am to all its old-schoolness. I like that there's no globally shared tagging, even if that means you party with a handful of randoms for 10 seconds and never speak to them again. I've even been fine with its archaic gathering quests, where all of its nodes are server-side instead of client-side. Want to go and pick that cactus fruit, but some other player beats you to it? Well, it's gone now. Go and pick another one.
Well, I was fine with it anyway. That is until I arrived in Orgrimmar, the Horde's capital city. My initial arrival was dizzying, bearing witness to its densely-populated streets and rapid-fire global chat where recruitment messages are quickly buried by folks talking about how many rolls of toilet paper they go through each day. Yeah, I dunno either.
(Image credit: Blizzard) I was having a lovely little time exploring, picking up just about every quest I could find. And then it happened. I innocently scooped up a quest called Rocks to Rest, tucked around the back of a building where a group of troll children are gathered.
Go and get some rocks so we can have chairs and tables, I'm ordered. Okay, easy enough. Right? WRONG.
Turns out that whimsical server-side gathering nodes become significantly less so when there are at least 10 of you vying for sporadically-spawning rocks. And you have to collect eight of the damn things. I scooped up my first one with relative ease, before the rest of my quest devolved into the chaos of rapidly swinging my camera around waiting for one to spawn, before watching everybody (me included) dash off in its direction for the hopes of being the chosen one who gets to loot it a millisecond before everybody else.
Now I've seen queues and orderly lines form for some of these quests, but Rocks to Rest? It's the wild west, baby. You snooze, you lose. I made the mistake of rotating my camera away from a rock that spawned directly behind me, and before I even had the chance to swing it back around and begin looting, I was beaten to the punch.
I was expecting a raid boss to be the thing that broke me. Maybe dying one too many times to a quest mob, or trying to navigate the game's multitude of systems as someone who has barely set foot in this world before. But no, it was a freaking boulder.

title: Kojima says his Sony split was amicable and they both still love us very much
text:
You do not, as a rule, see studios respond to rumours, reports, and speculation, but a recent Bloomberg report that Sony dropped Physint , Kojima Productions' upcoming stealth game, because it was overbudget and kept missing deadlines must have rankled the studio a little, because it released the statement above yesterday to quell fears.
To quell fears of what? Well, mostly that the relationship between Hideo Kojima and Sony has gotten as bad as the relationship between Hideo Kojima and Konami, his erstwhile employer. Sure, says the studio, they might have split on Physint, but it was amicable. They'll probably even still spend Christmas together.
Meanwhile, Xbox has swooped in for an easy PR win: picking up the cheque for Physint's continued development. All's well that ends well? We'll see.

text:

It's DDR5-5600 of ECC RDIMM in a 16-pack kit for precisely $101,451.99 at Amazon , for all you server engineers out there. But the question that has been burning my bonce is who is buying their server farm memory directly from Amazon?
